body_text: - Second quarter DAYBUE® GAAP net sales of $125 million, up 30% year-over-year driven by strong uptake of DAYBUE STIX - Second quarter NUPLAZID® GAAP net sales of $183 million, up 10% year-over-year on a non-GAAP adjusted basis - Increased full year 2026 total revenue guidance to $1.24 to $1.30 billion, reflecting higher DAYBUE guidance of $480 to $510 million and reaffirmed NUPLAZID guidance of $760 to $790 million - Topline results from the Phase 2 remlifanserin study in Alzheimer’s disease psychosis anticipated September to October 2026 SAN DIEGO—(BUSINESS WIRE)— Acadia Pharmaceuticals Inc. (Nasdaq: ACAD), today announced its financial results for the second quarter ended June 30, 2026. “Acadia delivered an outstanding second quarter, highlighted by strong commercial execution across both DAYBUE and NUPLAZID, resulting in total revenue growth of 17% year-over-year on an adjusted basis,” said Catherine Owen Adams, Chief Executive Officer of Acadia. “For DAYBUE, continued patient demand and robust uptake of STIX drove another quarter of strong performance. For NUPLAZID, we continued to see strong momentum, especially in new-to-brand prescriptions as our recently expanded sales force gained traction in the field. We remain confident that both franchises are on track to achieve our long-term ambition of approximately $1.7 billion in annual net sales in 2028. Looking ahead, we are excited about the anticipated topline results from our Phase 2 program evaluating remlifanserin in Alzheimer's disease psychosis in the September to October timeframe, which we believe represents a potentially transformational opportunity for Acadia.” Company Updates Completed enrollment in the Phase 2 portion of the RADIANT program evaluating remlifanserin in Alzheimer's disease psychosis and initiated Phase 3 screening and enrollment; topline Phase 2 results are expected in September to October 2026. Received FDA Fast Track designation for remlifanserin for the treatment of hallucinations and delusions associated with Alzheimer's disease psychosis, recognizing its potential to address a significant unmet medical need. The Committee for Medicinal Products for Human Use (CHMP) of the European Medicines Agency (EMA) adopted a positive opinion recommending marketing authorization for DAYBU ®(trofinetide) for the treatment of neurobehavioral symptoms of Rett syndrome in adults and pediatric patients aged five years and older. If approved by the European Commission, DAYBU would become the first authorized treatment for Rett syndrome in the European Union. Financial Results Revenues GAAP total revenues, comprised of net product sales from NUPLAZID and DAYBUE, were $308 million for the second quarter of 2026, up 16% as compared to GAAP total revenues of $265 million in the second quarter of 2025, and up 17% as compared to non-GAAP adjusted total revenues of $262 million in the second quarter of 2025. GAAP net product sales of NUPLAZID were $183 million for the second quarter of 2026, up 9% compared to GAAP net product sales of $168 million for the second quarter of 2025, and up 10% as compared to non-GAAP adjusted net product sales of $166 million for the second quarter of 2025. Net product sales of DAYBUE were $125 million for the second quarter of 2026, an increase of 30% as compared to $96 million for the second quarter of 2025. A reconciliation of NUPLAZID non-GAAP adjusted net product sales and non-GAAP adjusted total revenues is provided in Table 1. A description of these adjustments is included under ‘Non-GAAP Financial Measures.’ Research and Development Research and development expenses for the second quarter of 2026 were $82 million, compared to $78 million for the same period of 2025. Selling, General and Administrative Selling, general and administrative expenses for the second quarter of 2026 were $160 million, compared to $134 million for the same period of 2025. Net Income For the second quarter of 2026, Acadia reported net income of $32 million, or $0.18 per diluted share, compared to a net income of $27 million, or $0.16 per diluted share, for the same period in 2025. Cash and Investments At June 30, 2026, Acadia’s cash, cash equivalents, and investment securities totaled $956 million, compared to $820 million at December 31, 2025. Full Year 2026 Financial Guidance (GAAP): Acadia is updating its 2026 guidance: Total revenues revised to a range of $1.24 to $1.30 billion, up from the previous range of $1.22 to $1.28 billion. NUPLAZID net product sales in the range of $760 to $790 million. DAYBUE (including all forms of trofinetide) global net product sales in the range of $480 to $510 million, up from the previous range of $460 to $490 million. R&D expense in the range of $355 to $380 million, down from the previous range of $385 to $410 million. SG&A expense in the range of $660 to $700 million. Conference Call and Webcast Information Acadia will host a conference call to discuss the second quarter 2026 results today, Tuesday, August 4, 2026 at 1:30 p.m. PT/4:30 p.m. ET. The conference call may be accessed by registering for the call here . Once registered, participants will receive an email with the dial-in number and unique PIN number to use for accessing the call. About NUPLAZID® (pimavanserin) Pimavanserin is a selective serotonin inverse agonist and antagonist preferentially targeting 5-HT2A receptors. These receptors are thought to play an important role in neuropsychiatric disorders. In vitro, pimavanserin demonstrated no appreciable binding affinity for dopamine (including D2), histamine, muscarinic, or adrenergic receptors. Pimavanserin was approved for the treatment of hallucinations and delusions associated with Parkinson’s disease psychosis by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration in April 2016 under the trade name NUPLAZID. About DAYBUE® (trofinetide) Trofinetide is a synthetic version of a naturally occurring molecule known as the tripeptide glycine-proline-glutamate (GPE). The mechanism by which trofinetide exerts therapeutic effects in patients with Rett syndrome is unknown. Trofinetide was approved for the treatment of Rett syndrome in adults and pediatric patients 2 years of age and older by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration in March 2023 under the trade name DAYBUE or DAYBUE STIX. About Acadia Pharmaceuticals Acadia is committed to turning scientific promise into meaningful innovation that makes the difference for underserved neurological and rare disease communities around the world. Our commercial portfolio includes the first and only FDA-approved treatments for Parkinson’s disease psychosis and Rett syndrome. We are developing the next wave of therapeutic advancements with a robust and diverse pipeline that includes mid- to late-stage programs in Alzheimer’s disease psychosis and Lewy body dementia psychosis, along with earlier-stage programs that address other underserved patient needs. title: Potain self-erecting crane reaches new heights on Norway mountaintop project
body_text: Contractor Hent faced the challenge of constructing a three-story restaurant on Fløya, a mountainous tourist destination overlooking the city of Tromsø in northern Norway. The new restaurant will sit at the summit station of the Fjellheisen cable car, 421 m above sea level, so Hent was seeking a versatile and reliable crane which could be installed quickly and operate efficiently in the remote and exposed environment. Norwegian Potain dealer Kranor suggested the Potain HDM 40, which has the right combination of performance and ease of installation, but once the crane choice was agreed, the trickier task of planning how to get it there began. “The only solution was to put the crane on two large skis and pull it up Fløya mountain with the support of two powerful snow groomers. Custom-built twin-tip skis were fitted to the crane’s chassis, allowing it to be pulled into position. Once in place, the crane was secured to the jobsite’s concrete foundation to ensure working stability in an area of strong winds. Getting the crane to the mountaintop is a truly unique logistics achievement,” explained Andreas Jensen, regional manager at Kranor . Designed to be three times the size of the previous structure, the new restaurant will feature an outdoor skywalk offering stunning views of the fjords and the Arctic landscape. It will also be a prime destination to observe the Northern Lights. Construction began last year and will finish in 2027.

title: Stop turning your best employees into the office help desk
summary: Your best employees are often your busiest, but the way they're spending their time leaves something to be desired. Learn how to take the pressure off your 'go-to people.'
body_text: Most managers worry about their lowest performers becoming a drag on the team. But some of the biggest productivity bottlenecks start at the other end of the spectrum. ​High performers naturally attract work. Everyone knows they’re good at their job, so they’re trusted to make decisions and answer questions. Every time they help, however, they make the team a little more dependent on them. Eventually, everyone else’s progress depends on access to a single person. ​Let’s be clear here: this isn’t a character flaw. There’s nothing wrong with employees who are generous with their time or willing to step in when others need help. The problem is a bigger, structural issue across the entire organization. Instead of establishing systems that make information and decisions accessible, the company has started routing them through the same handful of people. You don’t need to stop your best employees from helping. You need to create a setup where they don’t need to do it all the time. When knowledge is shared and easily accessible, everyone is clear who owns what task, and work can continue without constantly waiting on a single person, your top performers can finally focus on the work that only they can do. The myth of the indispensable employee Companies tend to celebrate indispensable employees, but resilient businesses learn not to depend on them. Sure, you need experts. Every team benefits from people with deep institutional knowledge or specialized skills. The problem comes from depending so heavily on that expertise that you can’t get work done without it. Researchers refer to this as knowledge concentration , and it’s when critical information is held by too few people. Software teams have a more colorful way of describing the concept: the “ bus factor ,” or “the minimal number of engineers that have to be hit by a bus for a project to be stalled.” Different terms, but the same idea. If losing one employee, even temporarily, would significantly disrupt your day-to-day operations, your company is too dependent on individual knowledge instead of shared systems. But depending on a few key people doesn’t just impact the timeline of certain projects, it also affects your daily productivity. According to McKinsey , knowledge workers spend almost half their workday collaborating with colleagues, customers, and partners rather than working independently. Every time an interaction requires waiting on the same person to answer a question or approve a decision, the delay ripples across the rest of the team. Work stops flowing between teammates and starts waiting in one person’s inbox. The irony is that the more indispensable someone becomes, the less time they have to focus on the work that requires their expertise. Instead of strategic thinking, your best employees spend their days answering routine questions and reviewing other people’s work, simply because they have become the company’s source of truth. Four signs you’ve created a human bottleneck Your strongest employees don’t want to be the cause of a bottleneck. They’re simply experiencing the downside of being a dependable, knowledgeable coworker.​ They’re responsive. They know where everything is. They catch mistakes before anything goes client-facing. Over time, more work starts going through them, because it’s almost always a guarantee of high quality. Here are a few signs this is already happening on your team. 1. They’re invited to almost every meeting. Take a look at your team’s calendar. Is there one person who seems to be at almost every planning meeting, kickoff, client call, and project check-in? It definitely depends on your circumstances and team size, but most of the time, a certain individual doesn’t need to be at every meeting their colleagues attend. 2. They’re the person everyone asks first. Every team has that person who gets messages like, “Where’s the latest version?” and “Can you take a quick look before I submit this?” All of the requests seem innocuous enough, but they’re the work equivalent of watching your kid stand in front of the closed fridge and ask if you have any milk. The answer already exists, they just know it’s faster to ask you than look for themselves. Those constant interruptions are a sign that your team has stopped looking for answers on their own. Either they’ve gotten too dependent on your strongest employee, or the answers they need aren’t accessible enough. On top of that, they make it hard for your strongest employee to experience any long stretches of focused work. 3. Work piles up while they’re on vacation. Some slowdown is inevitable when experienced employees are away, especially for the projects they’re involved in. But if work comes to a standstill because a single person is out, your workflow relies too heavily on them. 4. They become the default editor for every pitch deck Plus every proposal. Every blog post. Every marketing email. Unless we’re talking about an actual editor in the office, no one person should be expected to guarantee perfection. Your team is shifting accountability instead of taking it upon themselves and adding unnecessary steps to their work. How to break the cycle Most high performers (your go-to problem-solvers and subject matter experts) won’t ask for help until they’re already overwhelmed . By that point, everyone around them has already adjusted their own workflows to depend on that person’s availability. It can be hard to break the cycle and reroute everyone’s questions, but it’s necessary if you want to keep your strongest employees and create an independent, motivated team. Changing things up requires you to restructure how work is organized so that information, decisions, and processes don’t depend on a single person’s memory or availability. Here’s what this looks like in practice. Start documenting answers the first time they’re offered Too many disruptions stem from questions that have already been answered before. The average person at work is interrupted once every 2 minutes , which means you need to do all you can to limit interruptions and promote more focus time within your team. Stop the madness by treating recurring questions as a sign that something needs to be documented. Design a space where answers can live for the whole team to access. You can have your web developer whip up a searchable knowledge base, but it also doesn’t have to be anything fancy. A Google Docs folder or Slack channel works just as well. The best format will always be the one your team defaults to. This step doesn’t end with documentation. You may need to train your employees to seek out the information on their own instead of asking for help. If they’ve learned to default to your team expert instead of independently problem-solving, it’ll take a little time and reminding to learn new habits. Define who owns everything Sometimes bottlenecks are caused by uncertainty. If an employee doesn’t know who has the authority to approve a budget or make a product decision, they naturally escalate the work to the most experienced person available. In turn, that person has to make the decision, or spend their time finding out who should be involved in the process. Clear ownership saves your high achievers from playing middleman. Before projects begin, define who is responsible for making decisions, who should be consulted, and which situations genuinely require executive approval. When it’s in writing and clearly communicated, employees are less likely to create informal approval chains that slow everyone down. Distribute critical knowledge among several employees We’ve all heard the stories of an entire ecosystem dependent on one key employee. An internal system coded by one engineer. A critical machine that a single facilities manager knows how to fix. A payroll specialist who understands a complicated reporting process.​ It’s someone else’s funny anecdote until it becomes your unfortunate reality, and you realize an entire team depends on the knowledge of a single individual. When critical knowledge lives in one brain, every vacation, sick day, or resignation can slow you down or completely halt your progress. To reduce that risk, you need to identify the processes that would experience the most disruption if one employee became unavailable, and start creating backup capability . Cross-train workers, rotate responsibilities, document complex workflows, and occasionally have a couple other people perform the task just to be sure they completely understand how it’s done. Protect deep work This wouldn’t be a RescueTime article without at least mentioning the power of deep work . Your highest performers often do the most cognitively demanding work, but they’re also interrupted the most. These two realities don’t work well together. Encourage your entire team to block off chunks of time where they’re unavailable for routine questions, meetings, and messages. More importantly, normalize respecting those boundaries. If someone is in a focus block, their teammates should wait until they’re available to make contact. Protecting deep work benefits everyone, but it’s especially important for your strongest employees. The more time they spend reacting to interruptions, the less time they have for the complex, high-value work that made them your top performers in the first place. Build a team, not a bottleneck Most of us are all too familiar with the cliché dynamics of a high school group project: one high-achieving student naturally takes the reins, answers everyone’s questions, catches mistakes, and makes sure the final project gets turned in. Unfortunately, it’s common for this pattern to follow us well into adulthood and the workforce. Your strongest employees still end up carrying the rest of the team, and they can quickly become overwhelmed and burnt out from the weight of the pressure. The difference is that managers have the ability to change the system. By clarifying ownership and making knowledge accessible, you create a team that keeps moving forward without depending heavily on a single person. That’s the difference between a high-performing employee and a high-performing organization. ​

This presentation is consistent with recent changes in how management evaluates our financial and business performance, including the information currently reviewed by our chief operating decision maker. Consumer revenue includes revenue from financial products and services intended for individual consumers, including insurance, credit cards, loans, bank accounts and other products and services. Consumer revenue includes our previously reported Insurance, Credit cards, Loans and Emerging verticals product categories. SMB revenue includes revenue from financial products and services intended for SMBs, including loans, credit cards and other products and services. SMB revenue of $22.1 million was down 11% year-over-year, primarily due to continued pressures in organic search traffic, partially offset by an increase in business loan originations. free cash flow in conjunction with GAAP measures as part of our overall assessment of our performance, including the preparation of our annual operating budget and quarterly forecasts, to evaluate the effectiveness of our business strategies, and to communicate with our Board of Directors concerning our financial performance. Non-GAAP operating income (loss): We define non-GAAP operating income (loss) as income (loss) from operations adjusted to exclude depreciation and amortization, and further exclude (1) losses (gains) on disposals of assets, (2) acquisition-related costs, and (3) restructuring charges. We also reduce income from operations, or increase loss from operations, for capitalized internally developed software costs. Adjusted EBITDA: We define adjusted EBITDA as net income (loss) from continuing operations adjusted to exclude depreciation and amortization, interest income (expense), net, other gains (losses), net, and provision (benefit) for income taxes, and further exclude (1) losses (gains) on disposals of assets, (2) stock-based compensation, (3) acquisition-related costs, and (4) restructuring charges. The above items are excluded from our non-GAAP operating income (loss) and adjusted EBITDA measures because these items are non-cash in nature, or because the amounts are not driven by core operating results and renders comparisons with prior periods less meaningful. We deduct capitalized internally developed software costs in our non-GAAP operating income (loss) measure to reflect the cash impact of personnel costs incurred within the time period. We believe that non-GAAP operating income (loss) and adjusted EBITDA provide useful information to investors and others in understanding and evaluating our operating results and in comparing operating results across periods. Moreover, non-GAAP operating income (loss) and adjusted EBITDA are key measurements used by our management internally to make operating decisions, including those related to analyzing operating expenses, evaluating performance, and performing strategic planning and annual budgeting. However, the use of these non-GAAP measures have certain limitations because they do not reflect all items of income and expense that affect our operations. Non-GAAP operating income (loss) and adjusted EBITDA have limitations as financial measures, should be considered as supplemental in nature, and are not meant as substitutes for the related financial information prepared in accordance with GAAP. These limitations include the following: Non-GAAP operating income (loss) and adjusted EBITDA exclude certain recurring, non-cash charges, such as amortization of software, depreciation of property and equipment, amortization of intangible assets, and (losses) gains on disposals of assets. Although these are non-cash charges, the assets being depreciated and amortized may have to be replaced in the future, and non-GAAP operating income (loss) and adjusted EBITDA do not reflect all cash requirements for such replacements or for new capital expenditure requirements; Non-GAAP operating income (loss) and adjusted EBITDA exclude certain acquisition-related costs, including acquisition-related retention compensation under compensatory retention agreements with certain key employees, and acquisition-related transaction expenses; Non-GAAP operating income (loss) and adjusted EBITDA exclude restructuring charges primarily consisting of severance payments, stock-based compensation, employee benefits, and related expenses for impacted employees, as well as contract termination costs, associated with our restructuring plan implemented in 2024; Adjusted EBITDA excludes stock-based compensation, including for acquisition-related inducement awards, which has been, and will continue to be for the foreseeable future, a significant recurring expense in our business and an important part of our compensation strategy; and Adjusted EBITDA does not reflect interest income (expense) and other gains (losses), net, which include unrealized and realized gains and losses on foreign currency exchange, as well as certain nonrecurring gains (losses). Our warehouse line of credit is used to fund mortgage loans originated for sale, as any increase or decrease in our mortgage loans held for sale is substantially offset by a corresponding borrowing or repayment on our warehouse line of credit. Adjusted free cash flow is a key measurement used by our management internally to evaluate our business performance and overall liquidity. We believe that adjusted free cash flow provides useful information for investors and others for determining the amount of cash available for investment in our business, strategic opportunities, repurchasing stock, strengthening our financial position and other purposes, as well as evaluating our historical and prospective liquidity. A limitation of the utility of adjusted free cash flow as a measure of financial performance and liquidity is that adjusted free cash flow does not represent the total increase or decrease in our cash balance for the period. title: Mentorship vs Self-Learning: What is Better for BIM Learning? {{year}}
summary: Discover the best approach to learn BIM. Know what works better for every career stage and prepares you with industry-ready skills.
body_text: Why Does the Way You Learn BIM Affect Career Growth? The way people learn BIM impacts the way they apply it in real projects. The variation shows in confidence, speed, and accuracy with which they work. Let’s dive further into this: Practical Application: Learning through real-world projects helps professionals comprehend how BIM tools and workflows work in practice. Problem-Solving: Working through practical challenges helps professionals develop the ability to identify issues and find effective solutions. Confidence: Regular practice and communication can make individuals feel secure when using BIM tools and handling project responsibilities. Collaboration: BIM learning through team-based projects helps professionals understand how to communicate and coordinate with different disciplines. Industry Readiness: Exposure to BIM workflows helps people discover workplace expectations and apply their skills more effectively. Continuous Growth: A strong learning foundation makes it easier for professionals to adapt to new construction technology and evolving industry practices. What Can You Learn Through Self-Directed BIM Training? Self-guided BIM courses are a great way to gain a foundational knowledge of the technology. Here’s what you can learn and how it can shape your professional development: BIM Software: Online tutorials and courses can help you develop working knowledge of tools such as Revit, Navisworks , and Dynamo, along with their common applications. Model Creation: You can learn to create and modify BIM models, develop building elements, and understand how different components work together within a project. Documentation: Self-learning can help you understand how to generate drawings, schedules, sheets, and other project documents directly from a BIM model. BIM Workflows: Exploring BIM workflows can give you a better understanding of how models, information, and documentation move through different stages of a project. Online Resources: You can use Udemy tutorials, blogs, forums, and BIM learning courses to explore specific tools, workflows, and concepts based on your upskilling needs. Personal Projects: Applying what you learn to small personal projects allows you to practise BIM workflows , experiment with different tools, and gradually build a portfolio of work. What Does Mentorship Add to BIM Learning? Mentorship gives learners an edge over their peers. It allows them to be sharper, more capable, and better prepared for real-world challenges. Here’s how it can help your career development: Expert Reviews: Mentors can examine your work, point out gaps, and suggest better ways to approach BIM tasks. Project Supervision: Working under expert insight helps learners understand how BIM skills are applied across different project stages. Industry Workflows: Mentors can introduce learners to workflows and practices commonly followed by BIM teams in professional settings. Model Review: Reviewing BIM models with an experienced professional can help learners spot errors, improve modelling practices, and understand project standards. Project Coordination : Mentors can help learners master how different disciplines coordinate their models and resolve design conflicts. Problem-Solving: Exposure to real project challenges helps learners develop practical ways to assess issues and make informed decisions. Mentorship vs Self-Learning: Which Works Better for Different BIM Career Stages? The right approach to BIM learning can vary depending on where you are in your engineering and architecture careers. Let’s explore how both methods offer distinct benefits at each career stage. Learning factor Self-learning Mentorship Best-suited for Getting started Learn basic BIM concepts and software at your own pace. Get a structured introduction with guidance from a skilled professional. Students and beginners Building software skills Practise BIM tools through tutorials and exercises. Learn software via project-based applications. Freshers Understanding workflows Explore BIM workflows using online resources. Understand how BIM workflows are used in projects. Early-career professionals Improving existing skills Identify areas for improvement and practise them independently. Receive feedback on your work and learn better approaches. Mid-career professionals Handling complex projects Build new skills based on your career goals and interests. Gain insights on developing skills relevant to future roles. Professionals seeking growth Staying updated Follow new tools, tutorials, blogs, and industry resources independently. Learn about evolving practices and technologies from experts. All career stages Can Self-Learning Build Job-Ready BIM Skills Without Industry Guidance? Self-learning becomes a stepping stone for BIM upskilling but it cannot fully equip professionals to become industry ready. Here’s why self-study may not be enough on its own: Understanding Project Standards: Every company may follow different naming conventions, templates, libraries, and modelling standards. These nuances are hard to gauge from generic BIM learning resources. Working With Constraints: Real projects come with deadlines, budgets, and frequent design changes. Therefore, learning in isolation rarely prepares learners to balance these competing demands. Understanding Roles: BIM processes involve well-defined responsibilities across modelling, coordination, and management activities. Industry exposure helps learners understand where their role fits within the larger picture. Quality Expectations: A model can look technically correct and still fail to meet project needs. Industry direction can help learners understand the level of detail, consistency, and accuracy expected in professional deliverables. When Should BIM Professionals Seek a Mentor? When individuals reach the limits of self-learning, mentorship can help them move forward with structured academic and online BIM courses . Let’s explore some situations where advice can make a difference: Repeatedly struggling with the same BIM concepts can be a sign that you need expert advice to identify and correct gaps in your skillset. An overwhelming number of BIM learning programs can make it difficult to decide what to learn and in what order. Moving beyond software skills requires an understanding of the principles, standards, and practices that shape BIM projects. Discussing your approach with an experienced professional can reveal better ways to handle unfamiliar BIM tasks. Real project experiences offer lessons that are difficult to replicate through tutorials and self-study. How Can You Combine Self-Learning and Mentorship for Faster BIM Career Growth? Combining self-learning with mentorship allows professionals to learn at their own pace while benefiting from expert guidance when needed. Here’s how you can balance both: Build the Foundation: Use online tutorials, courses, and free resources to understand BIM concepts and develop basic software skills . Practise Independently: Apply your BIM learning on capstone projects to strengthen your understanding and become more comfortable with BIM tools. Seek Expert Input: Share your work with a mentor to identify gaps, improve your approach, and understand where you can develop further. Learn From Critique: Use feedback to revisit difficult concepts, correct mistakes, and improve your work instead of simply moving on to the next topic. Apply New Skills: Take the suggestions you receive and put them into practice while working on complex projects. Keep Learning: Continue using self-learning resources to explore new tools and techniques while turning to mentors when you need direction or practical insight. A mixed approach can make BIM learning more structured without taking away the flexibility of learning independently. For professionals looking for a more organized training, Novatr’s BIM Professional Program can provide a combination of thoughtful learning, projects, and industry exposure.

The distribution covers the period from July 1st through July 31st, 2026. title: Tuya Smart startet Tuya AI Coding und ermöglicht es Nutzern, eigene KI-gestützte Lifestyle-Apps mittels natürlicher Sprache zu erstellen
summary: /PRNewswire/ -- Tuya Smart (NYSE: TUYA; HKEX: 2391), ein globaler Anbieter von KI-Cloud-Plattformdiensten, hat offiziell „Tuya AI Coding" eingeführt – eine...
body_text: HANGZHOU, China , 5. August 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Tuya Smart (NYSE: TUYA ; HKEX: 2391), ein globaler Anbieter von KI-Cloud-Plattformdiensten, hat offiziell „Tuya AI Coding" eingeführt – eine KI-native No-Code-Plattform zur Anwendungsentwicklung, mit der Nutzer ihre Ideen mit nur einer einzigen Eingabe in KI-gestützte Lifestyle-Anwendungen umsetzen können. Indem sie ihre Ideen, gewünschten Funktionen oder Anforderungen an die Benutzeroberfläche in natürlicher Sprache beschreiben, können Nutzer Anwendungen generieren, die lauffähig und bereitstellbar sind und echte KI-gesteuerte Erlebnisse ermöglichen. Die Plattform unterstützt zudem die Bereitstellung mit einem Klick sowie das Teilen auf Social-Media-Plattformen. Die Einführung von Tuya AI Coding markiert einen weiteren Schritt in Tuyas Expansion von KI-generierten Seiten hin zu KI-Anwendungen, die mit der physischen Welt interagieren können, und erweitert damit die Möglichkeiten des AI-Home-Ökosystems. Die KI-Anwendungsentwicklung geht über die Seitenerstellung hinaus und hält Einzug in den Alltag Gartner hat KI-native Anwendungsentwicklungsplattformen zu einem der wichtigsten strategischen Technologietrends für 2026 gekürt und prognostiziert, dass bis zum Jahresende 75 % aller neuen Anwendungen weltweit mithilfe von Low-Code-Entwicklungsansätzen erstellt werden. Hinter diesem rasanten Marktwachstum zeichnet sich ein neuer Branchenwandel ab: Da die Hürden für die Entwicklung von KI-Anwendungen weiter sinken, verändert sich auch der Maßstab für die Bewertung des Nutzens dieser Anwendungen. Der Juli-Bericht von Frost & Sullivan stellte fest, dass sich KI-native No-Code-Plattformen zur App-Erstellung von der bloßen „Erstellung von Apps durch Konversation" hin zur „Ermöglichung einer vollständigen Geschäftsumsetzung" entwickeln, wobei sich der Wettbewerb mittlerweile über die reinen App-Erstellungsfunktionen hinaus auf Bereitstellung, Markteinführung, Betrieb und kontinuierliche Iteration ausweitet. Kurz gesagt: Bei der „letzten Meile" der KI-Anwendungsentwicklung geht es nicht mehr nur um die Generierung von Code – es geht darum, ob sich eine Anwendung in reale Szenarien integrieren lässt. Eine App, die auf den Browser beschränkt ist und nicht mit realen Diensten, Geräten oder Daten interagieren kann, hat nur einen begrenzten praktischen Wert. Genau diese Herausforderung soll Tuya AI Coding lösen. Die Plattform wurde entwickelt, um menschliche Kreativität nahtlos mit KI-Technologie zu verbinden, und ist so konzipiert, dass jede KI-generierte Anwendung vom ersten Tag an in der Lage ist, sich mit realen Geräten zu verbinden, echte Nutzer zu bedienen und reale Erfahrungen zu ermöglichen. Ideen mit einem einzigen Befehl in KI-Lifestyle-Anwendungen verwandeln Die meisten derzeit auf dem Markt erhältlichen Tools zur Erstellung von KI-Apps beschränken sich nach wie vor auf die digitale Welt und gehen nicht über die Erstellung von Webseiten oder Mini-Programm-Oberflächen hinaus. Tuya AI Coding basiert auf dem globalen KI+IoT-Technologie-Stack von Tuya und verfügt über drei grundlegende Kernfunktionen: Gerätekonnektivität, Cloud-Dienste und Datenintelligenz. Wenn Nutzer eine Anforderung eingeben, leistet die KI mehr als nur die Generierung von Schnittstellen und Interaktionslogik. Sie baut zudem automatisch die gesamte Backend-Architektur auf, einschließlich Datenbanken, API-Gateways, Benutzerauthentifizierung und Gerätemanagement, und stellt dabei eine direkte Verbindung zur Cloud-Infrastruktur von Tuya her, die sich über mehr als 200 Länder und Regionen erstreckt. Gleichzeitig nutzt Tuya AI Coding das umfangreiche KI-Hardware-Ökosystem von Tuya und bietet native Unterstützung für den Zugriff auf mehr als 100.000 SKUs. Grundlegende Funktionen wie Geräteverwaltung, Datenanalyse und Wetterinformationsdienste lassen sich flexibel hinzufügen und ermöglichen so eine nahtlose Integration zwischen Softwareanwendungen und realen Hardwaregeräten. Nicht-technische Kreative befähigen, KI-Lifestyle-Erlebnisse zu gestalten Tuya AI Coding richtet sich in erster Linie an kreative Nutzer ohne technischen Hintergrund, darunter Designer, Produktmanager, Unternehmer, Freiberufler und Studierende. Für diese Nutzer sind die wichtigsten Anforderungen bei der Entwicklung von KI-Anwendungen klar: Ideen schnell in funktionierende Produkte umzusetzen, technische Hürden zu senken, Konzepte kostengünstig zu validieren und ein Gefühl kreativer Erfüllung zu erlangen. Traditionelle Entwicklungsabläufe standen dem jedoch lange Zeit im Weg. Hohe technische Hürden, begrenzte Ressourcen, langsame Iterationszyklen und komplexe Tools hindern kreative Menschen oft daran, ihre Ideen zum Leben zu erwecken. Um diesen Herausforderungen zu begegnen, bietet Tuya AI Coding mehrere Kernfunktionen: Echtzeit-Vorschau und dialogbasierte Iteration: Während des Generierungsprozesses wird die Benutzeroberfläche in Echtzeit dargestellt, sodass Nutzer Details sofort durch Befehle in natürlicher Sprache wie „Mach den Button größer" oder „Füge einen Dunkelmodus hinzu" verfeinern können. Vorlagenbibliothek und szenariobasierte Unterstützung: Branchenspezifische Anwendungsfälle werden durch gebrauchsfertige Vorlagen unterstützt, was die Entwicklung zugänglicher und effizienter macht. Plattformübergreifende Kompatibilität und Bereitstellung mit einem Klick: Die Plattform generiert automatisch Anwendungen, die auf PCs, Smartphones, Tablets und anderen Geräten funktionieren, und ermöglicht gleichzeitig die Bereitstellung in der Cloud mit einem Klick sowie die einfache Freigabe auf Social-Media-Plattformen. Ein vollständiger „No-Code"-Workflow: Was bei der herkömmlichen Entwicklung einst Monate dauerte, lässt sich nun auf Minuten verkürzen, wodurch die technische Hürde um 90 % gesenkt wird. Da die KI-Branche einen tiefgreifenden Wandel in der Wertschöpfung durchläuft, wird „Kreativität für alle freizusetzen" genauso wichtig wie die Steigerung der Effizienz. Da immer mehr Plattformen die Möglichkeit bieten, Anwendungen mit einem einzigen Satz zu generieren, wird die Besonderheit von Tuya AI Coding immer deutlicher: Es generiert nicht nur KI-Anwendungen, sondern ermöglicht auch deren Integration in das KI-Hardware-Ökosystem von Tuya und beschleunigt so den Wandel in der realen Welt. Tuya AI Coding ist jetzt offiziell verfügbar. Nutzer können die Plattform unter coding.tuya.ai erkunden. Informationen zu Tuya Smart Tuya Smart (NYSE: TUYA ; HKEX: 2391) ist ein weltweit führender Anbieter von KI-Cloud-Plattformdiensten, der sich dafür einsetzt, KI in den Alltag zu integrieren. Durch sein Open-Source-Entwicklungsframework TuyaOpen und universelle KI-Agent-Engines, einschließlich der KI-Agent-Entwicklungsplattform, integriert Tuya multimodale KI-Funktionen, um Hindernisse für die KI-Entwicklung abzubauen, die Verwirklichung eines KI-gesteuerten Lebensstils effizient voranzutreiben und die Integration von KI in die physische Welt zu beschleunigen. Tuya bietet innovative physische KI-Lösungen für intelligente Geräte, kommerzielle Anwendungen und Entwickler in der Industrie durch seine Cloud-Computing- und räumlichen Intelligenzfunktionen. Darüber hinaus bietet das Unternehmen ein vollständiges, offenes und neutrales globales AIoT-Ökosystem. Dieser Ansatz fördert eine lebendige globale Entwickler-Community, die sich aus Marken, OEMs, KI-Agenten, Systemintegratoren und unabhängigen Softwareanbietern zusammensetzt, die zusammenarbeiten, um intelligente Lösungsökosysteme zu schaffen, die die Prinzipien der Nachhaltigkeit, Sicherheit, Effizienz, Agilität und Offenheit verkörpern. Zum 31. März 2026 zählte die Tuya AI Developer Platform über 1.970.000 registrierte KI-Entwickler aus mehr als 200 Ländern und Regionen.

title: Mengapa Ingin Kerja di Jepang? Ini Alasan Kuatnya
summary: Mengapa ingin kerja di Jepang? Temukan alasan kuat, keuntungan nyata, dan tips penting bagi kamu yang bermimpi berkarier di Negeri Sakura.
body_text: Pernahkah kamu tiba-tiba terpikir, “Kayaknya enak banget kalau bisa kerja di Jepang” ? Kalau iya, kamu tidak sendirian. Ribuan orang Indonesia setiap tahunnya memilih Jepang sebagai tujuan berkarier di luar negeri. Tapi apa sebenarnya yang membuat negara ini begitu menarik? Buat kamu yang sedang mempertimbangkan langkah besar ini, yuk kita bahas tuntas alasan-alasan kuatnya. Sebelum kamu memutuskan, penting banget untuk benar-benar paham motivasinya. Bukan cuma karena tren atau ikut-ikutan teman. Karena kerja di luar negeri itu butuh persiapan serius, mental yang kuat, dan alasan yang jelas supaya kamu bisa bertahan dan berkembang di sana. Daftar Isi Toggle Gambaran Umum Dunia Kerja di Jepang Jepang dikenal sebagai salah satu negara dengan etos kerja tertinggi di dunia. Budaya monozukuri (seni membuat sesuatu dengan penuh dedikasi) sudah meresap dalam DNA profesional mereka. Ini bukan sekadar klise, melainkan realita yang akan kamu rasakan sendiri ketika bekerja di sana. 1. Pasar Kerja yang Terus Terbuka untuk Tenaga Asing Jepang sedang menghadapi aging population , alias populasi yang menua dengan cepat. Akibatnya, banyak sektor industri kekurangan tenaga kerja produktif. Pemerintah Jepang pun aktif membuka pintu bagi pekerja asing melalui berbagai program resmi, termasuk program Tokutei Ginou (Specified Skilled Worker) yang menyasar banyak bidang industri. Artinya, peluang buat kamu sebagai orang Indonesia itu nyata dan terbuka lebar. Bukan hanya di bidang teknologi atau manufaktur, tapi juga di sektor perhotelan, pertanian, konstruksi, hingga perawatan lansia. 2. Gaji dan Standar Hidup yang Kompetitif Salah satu alasan paling jujur yang sering disebut orang ketika ditanya mengapa ingin kerja di Jepang adalah soal penghasilan. Standar upah di Jepang, bahkan untuk pekerjaan entry-level , umumnya jauh lebih tinggi dibandingkan upah di Indonesia untuk posisi serupa. Selain gaji pokok, banyak perusahaan di Jepang yang memberikan tunjangan tempat tinggal, transportasi, hingga makan. Ini membuat pengeluaran harianmu bisa lebih terkontrol, sehingga kamu punya potensi untuk menabung lebih banyak. 3. Sistem Kerja yang Terstruktur dan Profesional Jepang punya budaya kerja yang sangat terstruktur. Ada jenjang karier yang jelas, pelatihan yang sistematis, dan standar profesionalisme yang tinggi. Bagi kamu yang ingin berkembang secara profesional, lingkungan ini bisa jadi tempat tumbuh yang luar biasa. Kamu akan belajar disiplin waktu, komunikasi yang efektif, dan kualitas kerja yang tidak asal-asalan. Pengalaman ini akan jadi aset berharga sepanjang karier kamu, ke mana pun kamu melangkah setelahnya. Alasan Personal yang Sering Mendorong Orang Ingin Kerja di Jepang Di balik angka dan peluang karier, ada alasan-alasan yang lebih personal dan emosional. Dan ini sama validnya. Kenali alasanmu sendiri supaya motivasi kamu tetap kuat di tengah tantangan yang pasti akan datang. 1. Kagum dengan Budaya dan Gaya Hidup Jepang Banyak orang Indonesia tumbuh besar dengan anime, manga, atau makanan Jepang dan akhirnya jatuh cinta dengan budayanya. Rasa kagum ini sering menjadi benih pertama dari keinginan untuk tinggal dan bekerja di sana secara langsung. Dan itu bukan alasan yang sepele. Mencintai budaya tempat kamu bekerja akan membuat proses adaptasi jadi lebih mudah dan menyenangkan. 2. Ingin Merasakan Pengalaman Hidup Mandiri di Luar Negeri Ada kepuasan tersendiri ketika kamu bisa hidup, bekerja, dan menghidupi dirimu sendiri di negara orang. Pengalaman ini menempa kemandirian, kemampuan problem-solving, dan kepercayaan diri yang tidak bisa didapat dari buku atau kelas manapun. Banyak diaspora Indonesia yang menyebutkan bahwa pengalaman kerja di luar negeri benar-benar mengubah cara pandang mereka terhadap hidup dan diri sendiri. 3. Ingin Mendukung Keluarga di Indonesia Tidak sedikit yang memilih kerja di Jepang demi bisa mengirim uang ke keluarga di tanah air. Ini motivasi yang mulia dan sangat nyata. Dengan penghasilan yang lebih tinggi, kamu bisa membantu biaya pendidikan adik, perawatan orang tua, atau bahkan membangun rumah. Untuk kebutuhan ini, layanan pengiriman uang internasional yang cepat dan andal seperti Transfez bisa sangat membantu kamu mentransfer uang ke Indonesia dengan mudah dari Jepang. 4. Ingin Memperluas Jaringan dan Wawasan Global Bekerja di Jepang artinya kamu akan berinteraksi dengan rekan kerja dari berbagai negara, belajar bahasa baru, dan memahami cara berpikir yang berbeda. Jaringan internasional yang kamu bangun ini akan sangat berguna jika suatu saat kamu ingin memulai bisnis atau pindah ke negara lain. Hal yang Perlu Kamu Siapkan Sebelum Berangkat Mimpi kerja di Jepang memang indah, tapi perjalanannya butuh persiapan yang matang. Jangan sampai kamu berangkat tanpa bekal yang cukup, karena itu justru bisa membuatmu kesulitan di sana. 1. Kuasai Bahasa Jepang Minimal Level Dasar Ini nyaris tidak bisa ditawar. Jepang bukan negara yang sangat ramah bagi mereka yang hanya mengandalkan bahasa Inggris, terutama di lingkungan kerja yang lebih tradisional. Minimal kamu perlu menguasai bahasa Jepang level JLPT N4 atau bahkan N3 agar bisa berkomunikasi sehari-hari dengan lancar. 2. Pahami Jalur Legal yang Tersedia Ada berbagai jalur resmi untuk bisa kerja di Jepang: program magang ( Technical Intern Training Program ), program pekerja terampil ( Specified Skilled Worker ), hingga jalur langsung melalui perusahaan yang membuka rekrutmen internasional. Pastikan kamu memilih jalur yang sesuai dengan latar belakang dan kemampuanmu. Kamu bisa mulai riset dari artikel tentang cara mencari pekerjaan di luar negeri sebagai panduan awal. 3. Siapkan Dokumen Penting Sejak Dini Mulai dari paspor yang masih aktif, sertifikat keahlian, hingga dokumen pendukung lainnya. Proses administrasi untuk bekerja di Jepang bisa memakan waktu, jadi semakin cepat kamu mempersiapkannya, semakin baik. 4. Bangun Tabungan Darurat Sebelum Berangkat Biaya awal hidup di Jepang, seperti deposit apartemen, perlengkapan awal, dan transportasi, bisa cukup besar. Pastikan kamu punya simpanan yang cukup untuk bertahan di bulan-bulan pertama sebelum gaji pertama cair. Kalau kamu belum punya strategi menabung yang solid, ini saat yang tepat untuk mulai memikirkannya. Ini tentang pilihan hidup yang penuh konsekuensi, sekaligus penuh kemungkinan luar biasa. Kalau kamu tahu dengan jelas mengapa ingin kerja di Jepang , itu akan jadi kompas yang mengarahkan setiap langkah persiapanmu. Semangat, dan semoga mimpimu segera jadi kenyataan! title: The Best Large SUVs for Gas Mileage in 2026
summary: Large SUVs and great gas mileage don't tend to go hand-in-hand. That said, some models are more impressive than others. Here are our favourites, including the BMW X7 and Chevrolet Tahoe.
body_text: When you need to move a lot of people and their things, or tow a heavy trailer, nothing beats the sheer size and capability of a large SUV. For a long time, accepting this utility meant accepting a hefty fuel bill as an unavoidable trade-off. These vehicles are, by their nature, big and heavy, two major factors that work against fuel efficiency. However, as technology has advanced, automakers have found clever ways to make these giants a bit more moderate in their fuel consumption, saving you money at the pump without sacrificing the space and power you need. The key to finding a large SUV with good gas mileage is to look beyond just the traditional V8 engine. Today's most efficient large SUVs often feature advanced powertrains, including smooth and torquey diesel engines, mild-hybrid systems that give the gas engine a bit of an electric boost, or even plug-in hybrid (PHEV) variants that can handle daily errands on electricity alone. This guide highlights the large SUVs that best balance the demands of space and capability with the practical need for reasonable fuel economy, helping you find a vehicle that can handle family road trips and trailer towing without requiring a fuel stop at every other exit. What Makes CarGurus Best Cars Guides Different The Best Large SUVs for Gas Mileage Chevrolet Suburban Chevrolet Tahoe Ford Expedition Land Rover Range Rover Mercedes-Benz GLS BMW X7 GMC Yukon Lincoln Navigator Lexus LX Toyota Sequoia FAQs Shopping Tools Related Topics 1. Chevrolet Suburban CarGurus expert rating: 8.2 out of 10 CarGurus user rating: 4.5 out of 5 Percentage of Good and Great Deals available on CarGurus: 31.5% Overall CarGurus rating: 4.6 out of 5 Pros Cons Excellent performance from the diesel engine Ungainly size Impressive technology Expensive in every trim level Massively useful cargo space Skip the 24-inch wheels Big three-row SUVs aren't known for thrift at the pump, but the Chevrolet Suburban gives mileage-minded shoppers a smart workaround: the updated 3.0-liter Duramax turbodiesel inline-six. With 305 hp and 495 lb-ft of torque, it delivers strong everyday shove without leaning on high revs, and it's EPA-rated at 21 mpg city, 27 mpg highway, and 23 mpg combined. Pair that efficiency with the Suburban's standard 28-gallon fuel tank and you're looking at the potential for 700+ highway miles between fill-ups—exactly the kind of real-world road-trip advantage this class rarely offers. That fuel-sipping range comes in the same huge, family-ready package the Suburban name is known for, including 41.5 cubic feet of cargo space behind the third row, 93.8 cubic feet with the third row folded, and a max of 144.7 cubic feet with both rear rows down. For 2025, a major interior tech makeover also matters on long drives: every Suburban gets a crisp 17.7-inch infotainment touchscreen (plus an 11-inch driver display), and standard driver aids like automatic emergency braking and lane-keeping assist help reduce fatigue. The tradeoff is cost—pricing starts at $63,495 including destination—and you'll want to avoid the available 24-inch wheels if ride comfort is a priority on rough pavement. It's notably smooth and quiet for a diesel, and it's rated at up to 27 mpg on the highway—an especially useful advantage on long trips in a full-size, three-row SUV. Pair that efficiency with the Tahoe's 24-gallon fuel tank and you're looking at an estimated highway cruising range approaching 650 miles in the right configuration, while still keeping the towing capability many shoppers need (up to 8,400 pounds with the 5.3-liter V8, rear-wheel drive (RWD), and the Max Trailering package). The 2025 refresh also makes day-to-day driving easier, with a much more modern cabin built around a standard 17.7-inch touchscreen, plus available large driver displays; importantly, Chevy keeps key climate functions on physical controls. title: Construction Project Management: How Owner Teams Can Keep Consultants Aligned Throughout Every Project
summary: Learn how construction project management software helps owner teams coordinate consultants, streamline approvals, and keep projects on schedule.
body_text: Construction owner teams rarely lose time on a project because a decision was wrong. They lose time because the right consultant never saw the question in time to answer it, or because a drawing revision sat in someone's inbox while a submittal waited on it. Multiply that across an architect, a structural engineer, an MEP consultant, and a handful of specialty reviewers, all working from their own inbox and their own file version, and even a well run project accumulates delay from coordination alone. This is the problem construction project management software is built to solve for owner teams specifically, not contractors, not suppliers, but the owner side of the table that has to keep every consultant aligned from the first design meeting through the final closeout. Below is a closer look at why owner teams need a better way to manage consultant coordination, the features worth checking for in a coordination platform, how to actually select one, and the benefits that show up once every consultant is working from the same shared system. Why Owner Teams Need a Better Way to Manage Consultant Coordination Owner teams on a construction project typically coordinate with a wide range of consultants: architects, structural engineers, MEP engineers, interior designers, and often specialty consultants for acoustics, sustainability, or code compliance. Each consultant works on their own timeline, submits their own deliverables, and often uses their own tools to track progress. The owner team is left holding the pieces, expected to know at any moment which drawings are current, which submittals are pending review, and which decisions are still waiting on approval from someone else. Owner teams researching construction and project management software are usually trying to solve this exact problem: too many consultants, too many separate threads, and no single place that shows where a project actually stands. The coordination burden only grows heavier as a project moves past design and into construction. Requests for information start flowing between the contractor and the design team. Change orders require input from whichever consultant originally specified the item in question. A single unanswered email from an engineer can hold up a submittal that a contractor needs approved before work can continue on site. When these threads live in separate inboxes rather than a shared system, an owner team has no reliable way to see where a project is actually stuck, only that it has stalled somewhere. The cost of that lag rarely shows up as a single line item on a budget report. It shows up as a contractor idle on site waiting for an approved submittal, a permit application delayed because a consultant's stamped drawing was still sitting in review, or a change order that could have been avoided entirely if a spec question had been answered a week earlier. None of these costs get tracked back to consultant coordination specifically. They accumulate quietly as schedule slip and budget variance that nobody on the owner team can fully explain when leadership asks why a project is behind. Many owner teams still coordinate consultants the way they did on a single small project years ago: email chains, shared drives with inconsistent file naming, and status calls that summarize where things stood a week ago rather than where they stand today. That approach can carry a small owner team through one project. It does not scale to a team running several developments at once, where the same coordination gaps multiply across every active job. Coordination failure is usually what pushes a project past its deadline , and consultant misalignment is one of the most common places that failure begins. The project teams an owner assembles, from architects and design consultants down to design assist contractors , all need a shared point of reference for scope, schedule, and open items. Without one, the owner team becomes the default coordination layer by necessity, chasing updates instead of making decisions. Key Features to Look for in a Consultant Coordination Platform A consultant coordination platform is not the same thing as a general project management tool repurposed for construction. The features that matter most are the ones that keep every consultant, every deliverable, and every decision visible to the owner team without requiring someone to chase status updates manually. The right project management software construction owner teams should start with a single shared record of every consultant assigned to a project, along with their scope, their current deliverables, and the deadlines attached to each one. That record should update automatically as work moves forward, rather than depending on someone manually rekeying status into a separate tracker. Specification and document control matters just as much. When standardized specs reduce change orders across repeat developments , it is because everyone involved, the owner team, the consultants, and the contractor, is working from the same current version rather than an outdated file pulled from an old email thread. A platform worth adopting keeps specifications, drawings, and revisions in one place, with a clear record of who changed what and when. Beyond documents, look for: A shared timeline : every consultant's deliverables mapped against the project schedule, so an owner team can see which items are on track and which are at risk before they become a delay. Open item tracking : a running record of requests for information, submittals, and decisions still waiting on a response, with clear ownership for each one. Portfolio visibility : the ability to see coordination status across every active development, not just one project at a time, for owner teams managing more than a single job. Role based access : consultants see what is relevant to their scope, while the owner team retains full visibility across the entire project team. A construction project management software platform built around these features, such as the construction project management platform MerlinAI provides , gives owner teams a live picture of where a project actually stands rather than a summary that is already a week out of date by the time it reaches them. These features work best together rather than separately. A shared timeline is only useful if it connects to the same document control system referenced in submittals, and open item tracking only closes the loop if it is tied to the same consultant records that hold scope and contact information. Owner teams that piece together separate tools for each of these needs often end up rebuilding the same coordination gap they were trying to close in the first place, just spread across more logins instead of fewer. Selecting a Consultant Coordination Solution for Construction Owner Teams Choosing project management software for construction projects starts with being honest about where coordination actually breaks down today. For some owner teams, the biggest gap is visibility, not knowing where a consultant's deliverable stands until it is already late. For others, it is document control, chasing down which version of a drawing is current. The right solution depends on which of these gaps is costing the most time and money right now. It also helps to look at how other owner teams have approached similar coordination problems. Some developers are pulling procurement decisions in house rather than leaving trade partners to manage purchasing separately, for many of the same reasons that push owner teams toward centralized consultant coordination: visibility, accountability, and a single record everyone can trust. The two problems, procurement and consultant coordination, are different in the details but come from the same root cause, information spread across too many disconnected tools. Scale matters too. A platform that works well for a single project can fall apart once an owner team is tracking progress across several developments without being able to visit every site constantly. Before committing to a solution, it is worth asking whether it was actually built to handle a portfolio of projects, each with its own consultants and its own schedule, or whether it was designed for one project and is being stretched to cover more. Finally, weigh how much of the coordination burden a platform actually removes versus how much it simply relocates. A tool that requires an owner team to manually update project status, chase consultants for input, and reconcile conflicting file versions has not solved the underlying problem. It has just moved the same manual work into a nicer interface. The best test is whether the owner team spends less time chasing information after adopting the platform, not just whether the information technically lives in one place now. Adoption matters as much as feature selection. A platform that sits unused by half the consultant team provides no more visibility than the spreadsheet it replaced. Before rolling out a new system, it is worth confirming that it fits into how consultants already work, submitting deliverables, responding to requests for information, tracking revisions, rather than asking them to learn an entirely new process on top of their existing workflow. The owner teams that get the most value from a coordination platform are usually the ones that involve their key consultants early, rather than presenting the system as a finished decision after the fact. How Construction Owner Teams Benefit from Centralized Consultant Coordination When consultant coordination runs through one connected system, the benefits show up quickly. Requests for information get answered faster because everyone can see who owns the next step, rather than a question sitting unanswered in someone's inbox. Submittals move through review without the delay of someone manually forwarding a file to the next consultant in line. Decisions get documented as they happen instead of being reconstructed from memory weeks later when a dispute comes up. The benefit compounds for owner teams running more than one development at a time. A consistent coordination process, the kind that supports developers building multiple buildings the same way , means every new project starts from a proven structure rather than a blank page. Consultants already know how the owner team expects deliverables to be tracked and reviewed, because it is the same process they used on the last project. Centralized coordination also gives owner teams something that scattered email threads never could: an accurate, current view of where every project actually stands. Instead of asking a project manager to summarize status ahead of a leadership review, the owner team can see it directly, updated as consultants complete their deliverables and decisions get made. That shift, from reconstructing status after the fact to seeing it live, is what separates owner teams that manage consultants well from those that spend most of their time simply trying to find out where things stand. There is also a relationship benefit that is easy to overlook. Consultants who work with an owner team that runs a clear, consistent coordination process tend to prioritize that owner's projects, because the process itself is less frustrating than working with a team that requires constant chasing and rework. Over several projects, that reputation compounds. Reliable coordination becomes a reason a strong consultant chooses to keep working with a particular owner team ahead of other opportunities competing for the same attention. Frequently Asked Questions What is construction project management software for owner teams? Construction project management software for owner teams centralizes consultant coordination, document control, and project status into one connected system, replacing scattered emails, shared drives, and separate trackers with a single shared record everyone can see. How is consultant coordination different from contractor project management? Consultant coordination focuses on the design side of a project, architects, engineers, and specialty consultants, and the deliverables, revisions, and approvals that flow between them and the owner. Contractor project management typically tracks field execution. A strong platform connects both so nothing falls through the gap between design and construction. Can project management software construction owner teams use handle multiple projects at once? Yes, provided it was built for a portfolio rather than a single job. Owner teams managing several developments need visibility across every active project, not just the one currently in front of them, along with a consistent process that consultants can follow on each new job. What causes the most delays in consultant coordination? Unanswered requests for information, outdated drawing versions, and decisions that were never clearly documented are among the most common causes. Most of these come down to information living in disconnected tools rather than a shared system the whole project team can see. What should owner teams look for when evaluating project management software for construction? Look for a shared timeline for consultant deliverables, centralized document and specification control, open item tracking with clear ownership, and portfolio level visibility for teams running more than one project. A platform missing any of these still leaves a coordination gap to manage manually.

title: Menopause hormone therapy: questions to ask your provider
summary: Menopause hormone therapy (MHT) can be an effective option for treating perimenopause and menopause symptoms.
body_text: Menopause hormone therapy: questions to ask your provider Written by the Progyny Editorial Team. Reviewed by the Progyny Clinical Team — July 2026. Menopause hormone therapy (MHT) can be an effective option for treating perimenopause and menopause symptoms. If MHT is right for you, it will be individualized to your health, symptoms, and lifestyle. We’ve suggested questions you may wish to ask your menopause specialist or other healthcare provider about MHT. We recommend making a separate appointment from your annual exam to have a focused conversation about your symptoms. Types of MHT Am I a candidate for MHT based on my age, symptoms, and health and family history? If not, what are my options for non-hormone medicines or treatments? What type(s) of MHT do you recommend for me? What are the pros and cons of the different forms available? How do I use this form of MHT, and how often? If I take systemic MHT, can I also use vaginal estrogen? Can I use vaginal estrogen that does not contain progesterone? How does MHT differ from birth control hormones I may already take? Benefits How well can I expect MHT to help with my specific symptoms? How long does it take to get relief from symptoms? Does MHT have other benefits outside of symptom relief? Risks and cautions What risks come with MHT, in my case? Can you put any risks into perspective? For example, how does this risk compare with the risk if I were not on MHT? Is there anything I can do to lower my risk? What side effects can happen, and how can I ease them? Broader care plan How long should I be on this therapy? If my symptoms improve, can I stop taking MHT? What should I do if my symptoms worsen or new ones start? What other lifestyle changes and/or treatments can I use along with MHT? When should I follow up with you? Alternatives to MHT What medicine, supplements, or lifestyle changes can I try instead? Tips for talking with your provider Your time with your provider may be limited, and they may share a lot of information. It’s always OK to ask them to explain something again if anything wasn’t clear. And it can be helpful to repeat back what your provider said in your own words to be sure you’ve got it. Your Progyny Care Advocate is here to offer support and help you prepare for your provider visits. You can also ask us to recommend websites and information to help you manage this transition. title: Paolla Oliveira and Fabiula Nascimento Star in 'Imperfect Mother,' Netflix's New Melodrama, Which Begins Shooting in Rio de Janeiro
body_text: São Paulo, August 19, 2026 - Netflix has announced that filming has begun on Imperfect Mother , a new melodrama series starring Paolla Oliveira and Fabiula Nascimento , directed by Rogério Gomes, better known as Papinha, in his first project with Netflix. Filmed in Rio de Janeiro, the series focuses on human relationships shaped by moral dilemmas, difficult choices and the challenges of starting over. Imperfect Mother , produced by A Fábrica based on an original idea by Eduardo Vaisman and Alice Gomes, is created by Felipe Sant'Angelo, Leonardo Moreira and Mariana Mesquita. Rogério Gomes (Papinha) serves as overall director, with João Gomez and Dayse Amaral Dias also directing. Felipe Sant'Angelo is the lead writer, sharing writing duties with Alice Gomes, Cauê Laratta, Maiara de Paula, Mariana Mesquita and Rodrigo Batista. Cecília Grosso is the producer, with Eduardo Vaisman, Katiuscha Mello and Mônica Juncken serving as executive producers. The main cast also includes Ailton Graça , Aline Borges , Denise Weinberg , David Junior, Emílio de Mello, Felipe Abib , Juliane Araújo , Mariana Molina , Renato Livera and Totia Meireles. (Credits: Erik França/ Netflix) This is Paolla’s third project with Netflix, following Turn of the Tide and The Stranger in My Bed ( release date TBA ), while this marks Fabiula’s first project with Netflix. About A Fábrica Founded in 2016, A Fábrica is part of Banijay Entertainment, one of the world’s largest media and entertainment groups. Led by partners Luiz Noronha, Cecilia Grosso, Samanta Moraes and Alberto Elias, the company has established itself as a leading creator and producer of premium content for film, television, streaming platforms and, more recently, vertical-format microdramas. Its portfolio includes a number of successful titles in Brazil and internationally, including the feature films My Life On Mars, Airplane Mode, Double Dad, Lulli, A Cut Above , and Wedding Games ; the series Galera FC and #NoFilter ; the documentary Son of a Mother ; the true-crime drama From Dreams to Tragedy: The Fire that Shook Brazilian Football ; the company is also behind Desperate Lies , the first Brazilian production to reach No. 1 globally on Netflix among non-English titles, and Vai Que Cola , the most-watched pay-TV comedy series in Brazilian history. Its most recent productions include the series Just the Two of Us and the feature film The Stranger in My Bed , both for Netflix. title: Galectin Therapeutics Announces Conversion of $105.8 Million in Debt to Equity, Significantly Strengthening Balance Sheet
summary: The Investor Relations website contains information about Galectin Therapeutics Inc.'s business for stockholders, potential investors, and financial analysts.
body_text: Chairman Richard E. Uihlein converts outstanding notes under five line of credit facilities into common stock Transaction eliminates approximately $105.8 million in debt and increases market capitalization NORCROSS, Ga., Aug. 04, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Galectin Therapeutics Inc. (NASDAQ: GALT) ("Galectin" or the "Company"), a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company developing therapies that target galectin-3 for the treatment of liver fibrosis and portal hypertension associated with MASH cirrhosis, today announced that Richard E. Uihlein, the Company’s Chairman of the Board and largest stockholder, has converted all outstanding principal and accrued interest under five of the Company’s line of credit facilities into shares of the Company’s common stock, effective July 31, 2026. The conversion eliminated approximately $105.8 million in total debt obligations including the related accrued interest in exchange for the issuance of 34,376,167 shares of common stock to Mr. Uihlein. The conversion covers all outstanding convertible promissory notes issued under the Company’s Line of Credit Letter Agreement dated July 25, 2022, and supplemental facilities dated March 29, 2024, November 14, 2024, March 31, 2025, and July 8, 2025. “This conversion represents a transformative event for Galectin’s balance sheet and financial position,” said Joel Lewis, Chief Executive Officer of Galectin Therapeutics. “By eliminating over $105 million in debt, we have dramatically improved our capitalization and strengthened our ability to advance our strategy and operations. Mr. Uihlein’s decision to convert his debt to equity reflects his unwavering commitment to the Company and his confidence in our galectin-3 inhibitor platform. I thank Mr. Uihlein once again for his continued support of the Company and our mission to advance belapectin to address a very large unmet medical need for patients with MASH cirrhosis and portal hypertension.” A sixth facility from the Supplemental Line of Credit Agreement dated December 19, 2025, providing for up to $10 million in additional financing has not been drawn upon and remains available to the Company. No convertible promissory notes have been issued under that facility, and it is unaffected by the conversion. Transaction Highlights: Elimination of approximately $105.8 million in total debt, consisting of $91.0 million in principal and approximately $14.8 million in accrued interest Issuance of 34,376,167 shares of common stock to Mr. Uihlein upon conversion Conversion covers all notes under five of six credit facilities; the December 2025 facility remains undrawn and available Significant strengthening of the Company’s balance sheet Demonstrates continued strong support from the Company’s Chairman and largest stockholder The conversion was effected pursuant to pre-existing conversion rights under convertible promissory notes issued to Mr. Uihlein in connection with the Company’s Line of Credit Letter Agreement dated July 25, 2022, and the Supplemental Line of Credit Agreements dated March 29, 2024, November 14, 2024, March 31, 2025, and July 8, 2025. Each note was converted at its specified conversion price (equal to the closing price of the common stock on the date of the note, subject to a $3.00 per share floor), resulting in a blended average conversion price of approximately $3.07 per share. Following the conversion, the Company had 100,849,644 shares of common stock outstanding as of July 31, 2026. The shares were issued in reliance upon the exemption from registration provided by Section 3(a)(9) of the Securities Act of 1933, as amended. The Company is obligated to register the resale of the shares within 180 days of the conversion date pursuant to the registration rights provisions in the line of credit agreements. About Galectin Therapeutics Galectin Therapeutics is dedicated to developing novel therapies to improve the lives of patients with chronic liver disease and cancer. Galectin’s lead drug belapectin is a carbohydrate-based drug that inhibits the galectin-3 protein, which is directly involved in multiple inflammatory, fibrotic, and malignant diseases, for which belapectin has Fast Track designation by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration. The lead development program is in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) with cirrhosis and portal hypertension, the most advanced form of MASH-related fibrosis. Liver cirrhosis is one of the most pressing medical needs and a significant drug development opportunity. Additional development programs are in treatment of combination immunotherapy for advanced head and neck cancers and other malignancies. Advancement of these additional clinical programs is largely dependent on finding a suitable partner. Galectin seeks to leverage extensive scientific and development expertise as well as established relationships with external sources to achieve cost-effective and efficient development. Additional information is available at www.galectintherapeutics.com.
